title: The purpose of risk management
blurb: Explain why projects manage risk, what it achieves, and what it can never promise.
question: A sponsor asks why the project manager is spending time on risk workshops when 'nothing has gone wrong yet'. What is the purpose of risk management, and what should the project manager NOT claim it will do?

teach.body: The purpose of risk management is to identify, assess and respond to risk so as to increase the likelihood of achieving the project's objectives. In plain English: spot what might go differently from the plan, work out which uncertainties matter most, and act early, so that threats do less damage and opportunities are not missed.

steps.label: Uncertainty
steps.sub: Things that might happen, good or bad

teach.h: What risk management gives a project

root.label: Purpose of risk management
root.sub: increase the likelihood of meeting objectives

teach.caption: Opportunities are half the purpose: a process that only hunts threats is doing half the job.

teach.body: Risk management looks ahead. It deals with events BEFORE they happen, while there is still time to change the plan, buy cover, add a reserve or seize an upside. That is what separates it from firefighting. Once something has actually happened, it is no longer a risk to be managed but a problem to be resolved.

teach.h: Worked scenario: the hospital car park
teach.body: At concept stage the team spots that the ground survey might reveal poor drainage. Because the threat is known early, the definition-stage budget includes a contingency and the sponsor approves the business case knowing the exposure. The team also spots that a council road scheme next door might share the same contractor, cutting mobilisation costs, and agrees to pursue it. Neither event has happened, but decisions are already better informed.

teach.h: Risk management runs through the life cycle

items.label: Early risks shape the business case

teach.caption: It is a continuous activity, not a one-off workshop at the start.

teach.h: What risk management does, and does not, do

rows.label: Improves the chance of meeting objectives
Removes all risk from the project

teach.note: Uncertainty is part of every project. The aim is to manage it to an acceptable level, not to eliminate it.

teach.text: Any option that says risk management 'eliminates all risk', 'guarantees success' or 'prevents all issues' is wrong. Equally wrong: 'it is only about threats'. The right answer always talks about improving the LIKELIHOOD of achieving objectives.

items: Purpose: identify, assess and respond to risk to increase the likelihood of achieving objectives.
It minimises threats AND maximises opportunities.
It supports informed decisions, realistic plans and sensible contingency.
It is proactive and continuous across the life cycle.
It cannot remove all risk, and it does not stop issues occurring.

summary: You can now explain that risk management exists to increase the likelihood of achieving objectives by minimising threats and maximising opportunities. You can also spot the false promises the exam uses as distractors: removing all risk, guaranteeing success or preventing every issue.

A.q: What is the main purpose of risk management on a project?
options: To remove every possible risk before work starts
To raise the likelihood of achieving objectives
To record problems after they have occurred
To pass all risk to suppliers through contracts
A.why: Risk management identifies, assesses and responds to risk to increase the likelihood of achieving the project's objectives.

whyNot.0: No project can remove every risk; the aim is to manage uncertainty, not eliminate it.
whyNot.2: Recording problems that have occurred is issue management, which is reactive.
whyNot.3: Transfer is one possible response to some threats, not the purpose of the whole discipline.

A.q: Why is risk management described as proactive?
options: It acts on events before they happen
It begins only when a problem occurs
It is carried out once, at project closure
It is led by the sponsor, not the team
A.why: Risk management anticipates uncertain future events and acts before they occur, while there are still options.

whyNot.1: Waiting for a problem to occur is reactive; that is the territory of issue management.
whyNot.2: Risk management runs throughout the life cycle, not only at closure.
whyNot.3: Who leads it has nothing to do with whether it is proactive.

A.q: Which statement about risk management is correct?
options: It guarantees the project will meet its budget
It prevents any issues from occurring
It deals only with threats to objectives
It also helps a project capture opportunities
A.why: Risk management aims to minimise threats and also to maximise opportunities.

whyNot.0: No process can guarantee the budget will be met; it improves the odds.
whyNot.1: Risk management reduces the chance and effect of problems but cannot stop issues occurring.
whyNot.2: Opportunities are part of risk, so risk management covers them too.

B.q: Which of the following is a benefit of risk management for decision-making?
options: Decisions can be left until project closure
Choices are made with the risks understood
The sponsor no longer needs to make decisions
Uncertainty is removed so no judgement is needed
B.why: By identifying and assessing risks, risk management lets the sponsor and team make choices knowing the likely threats and opportunities.

whyNot.0: Deferring decisions to closure would defeat the point of acting early.
whyNot.2: Risk management informs the sponsor's decisions; it does not replace them.
whyNot.3: Uncertainty can be managed but not removed, so judgement is still needed.

B.q: Complete the statement: risk management cannot remove all risk, and it does not ______.
options: help to set a sensible contingency
support realistic project plans
stop issues occurring on a project
consider opportunities as well as threats
B.why: Some risks will still occur and new problems will arise, so risk management cannot stop issues occurring.

whyNot.0: Setting a sensible contingency is one of the things risk management does help with.
whyNot.1: Supporting realistic plans is a genuine purpose of risk management.
whyNot.3: Considering opportunities as well as threats is part of its purpose.

B.q:
Which TWO of the following are purposes of risk management?
1. Minimising threats to objectives
2. Guaranteeing project success
3. Maximising opportunities
4. Removing the need for a plan
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Risk management aims to minimise threats and maximise opportunities, so that objectives are more likely to be met.

whyNot.0: Minimising threats is right, but nothing can guarantee success.
whyNot.2: Neither guaranteeing success nor removing the plan is a purpose of risk management.
whyNot.3: Maximising opportunities is right, but risk management supports the plan rather than replacing it.

C.q: A team spots that early delivery by a supplier could let them finish a month sooner, and plans how to make the most of it. Which purpose of risk management does this show?
options: Recording an issue that has occurred
Capturing an opportunity as well as threats
Removing all uncertainty from the schedule
Passing schedule risk to the supplier
C.why: Planning to make the most of an uncertain upside is maximising an opportunity, a core purpose of risk management.

whyNot.0: Nothing has happened yet, so this is not an issue.
whyNot.2: The delivery date is still uncertain; planning for it does not remove uncertainty.
whyNot.3: The team is pursuing a benefit, not handing a threat to someone else.

C.q: A sponsor says: 'Now we have a risk register, nothing can go wrong.' What is the best response?
options: Agree, as all known risks are now removed
Agree, as issues cannot arise once risks are logged
Disagree, as only threats appear on a register
Disagree, as risk is managed but never eliminated
C.why: Risk management improves the odds of success but cannot eliminate uncertainty; risks can still occur and new problems can arise.

whyNot.0: Logging a risk does not remove it; responses reduce or manage it.
whyNot.1: Issues can still arise, both from risks that occur and from events nobody foresaw.
whyNot.2: This is the wrong reason: a register records opportunities as well as threats.

C.q: Why does risk management continue throughout the life cycle rather than only at the start?
options: New risks emerge and existing ones change
The risk register must be rewritten each week
Risks can only be closed during deployment
The sponsor needs a new business case per phase
C.why: Circumstances change: new risks appear, others grow, shrink or pass, so responses must be kept current through to closure.

whyNot.1: The register is updated as needed, not rewritten weekly by rule.
whyNot.2: Risks can be closed whenever they pass or occur, at any point in the life cycle.
whyNot.3: The business case is refined at gates, but that is not why risk management is continuous.

reteach.title: Packing for a family camping trip
reteach.question: A family is planning a week of camping in the Lake District. Why does it pay to think about what might happen before they leave, rather than once they arrive?

blocks.body: Before leaving they ask what might happen. Rain is likely, so they pack waterproofs and a spare tarpaulin. A campsite might cancel, so they note a backup site. A clear evening might give the chance to see the stars, so they pack binoculars. None of this stops it raining. It simply means the holiday is far more likely to go well, whatever happens.

blocks.text: Thinking ahead did not stop the rain. Risk management never removes uncertainty: it makes the objective (a good holiday) more likely.

explain.body: Identify, assess and respond to risk so as to increase the likelihood of achieving objectives. Everything else risk management does flows from this one aim.

test.q: Complete the statement: the purpose of risk management is to increase the ______ of achieving the project's objectives.
options: likelihood
overall cost
delivery speed
agreed scope
test.why: Risk management aims to increase the likelihood of achieving objectives.

whyNot.1: Risk management does not aim to increase overall cost; it often protects the budget.
whyNot.2: Delivery may speed up, but the purpose is framed around the likelihood of success.
whyNot.3: Increasing the agreed scope is not a purpose of risk management.

explain.body: Risk management minimises threats (making them less likely or less damaging) and maximises opportunities (making them more likely or more valuable). A process that ignores opportunities leaves value on the table.

test.q: What should risk management aim to do with opportunities?
options: Ignore them, as they cause no harm
Record them as issues to be resolved
Transfer them to a third party
Maximise their chance and benefit
test.why: Risk management seeks to maximise opportunities: make them more likely and their benefit greater.

whyNot.0: Ignoring opportunities misses half the purpose of risk management.
whyNot.1: An opportunity has not happened, so it is not an issue.
whyNot.2: Transfer is a threat response; for opportunities the partnering response is 'share'.

explain.body: Risk management acts on events before they happen, while there is time to change the plan or prepare. Once a threat materialises it becomes a problem to resolve, which is the job of issue management.

test.q: Which word best describes the nature of risk management?
options: Reactive
Retrospective
Proactive
Optional
test.why: Risk management is proactive: it anticipates uncertain events and acts before they occur.

whyNot.0: Reacting after an event is closer to issue management.
whyNot.1: Looking back is what reviews and lessons learned do, not risk management's main job.
whyNot.3: Risk management is a core part of managing any project, not an optional extra.

explain.body: Risk management cannot remove all risk, cannot guarantee success and does not stop issues occurring. It manages uncertainty to an acceptable level and gives the project the best realistic chance.

test.q: Which of the following is a realistic claim about risk management?
options: It ensures no threat will ever occur
It guarantees every objective is met
It makes success more likely, not certain
It replaces the need for issue management
test.why: Risk management improves the likelihood of success but can never make it certain.

whyNot.0: Threats can still occur despite good responses.
whyNot.1: Nothing can guarantee every objective is met.
whyNot.3: Problems still arise, so issue management is still needed.
